title: Transport of normalized tensor constraints through coherent realization
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi$, and schemes $W$ on which $\ell$ is invertible [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension, def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. On each small pro-etale site set $B_{W,n}=(\mathcal O_E/\varpi^n)_W$ for $n\ge1$ and $R_W=\lim_n B_{W,n}$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Work in the ordinary unbounded derived category $\mathscr D_W=D(\mathscr S(B_{W,\bullet}))$ of whole semilinear systems, with its tensor and geometric inverse image [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. A normalized system has invertible transition adjoints $\alpha^A_{m,n}:q_W^*A_m\to A_n$, where $q_W^*=-\otimes^L_{B_{W,m}}B_{W,n}$, for all $m\ge n\ge1$, with the identity and quotient cocycles [def-coef-normalized-dvr-tower]. For systems $A,N$ on $W$ and $C$ on $Y$, write $T_W(A,N)_n=A_n\otimes^L_{B_{W,n}}N_n$, $F_f(C)_n=Lf_n^*C_n$ for $f:X\to Y$, and $U_W=(B_{W,n}[0])_n$, with the induced whole-system transitions.

Write $\mathcal R_WK=(K\otimes^L_{R_W}B_{W,n})_n$ for coherent reduction [def-weil-integral-reduction-tower] and $\mathcal L_W=R\lim\operatorname{Res}$ for total derived limit of the restricted whole system [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]. Use the canonical adjunction $\mathcal R_W\dashv\mathcal L_W$ and its natural counit $e_A:\mathcal R_W\mathcal L_WA\to A$ [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus], invertible for normalized $A$ [lem-coef-normalized-dvr-effectivity]. Let $\widehat T_W,\widehat F_f$ be the actual quotient-complex/Roos completed operations [def-pur-integral-derived-operations].

For finite typed expressions $P$ with input locations and constructors input, coefficient unit, tensor and scheme pullback [def-pur-completed-operation-expressions], let $S_P$ evaluate in $T,F,U$ on normalized inputs, and let $K_P$ evaluate in $\widehat T,\widehat F,\mathcal LU$ on their limits. Define $\beta_P:K_P\to\mathcal L S_P$ recursively by identities at inputs and units, $\beta_{T(P,Q)}=\beta_T(S_P,S_Q)\circ\widehat T(\beta_P,\beta_Q)$ and $\beta_{F_f(P)}=\beta_F(S_P)\circ\widehat F_f(\beta_P)$. Here the primitive maps are those of [lem-pur-completed-primitive-counit-comparison]: the defining quotient realization followed by $\mathcal L T(e_A,e_N)$ and $\mathcal L F_f(e_C)$, respectively. Put $\gamma_P=e_{S_P}\circ\mathcal R(\beta_P)$.

Let $A,N,H$ be arbitrary normalized systems on one $W$. The canonical total-complex maps
$$(x\otimes y)\otimes z\mapsto x\otimes(y\otimes z),\quad b\otimes x\mapsto bx,\quad x\otimes b\mapsto bx,\quad x\otimes y\mapsto(-1)^{pq}y\otimes x$$
for homogeneous degrees $p,q$ define natural isomorphisms $a:S_P\to S_Q$ of whole systems for the expression pairs $(T(T(A,N),H),T(A,T(N,H)))$, $(T(U_W,A),A)$, $(T(A,U_W),A)$ and $(T(A,N),T(N,A))$, respectively, with each named system regarded as an input expression. They commute with every actual quotient transition. The scalar-extension compatibility is that of the canonical tensor comparison [lem-pur-cochain-pullback-tensor-coherence]; for an arbitrary normalized transition the square is composed with naturality in its adjoint $\alpha_{m,n}$. In particular the reassociation routes both take three homogeneous inputs to the tensor of the same three images, the action routes multiply the same scalar, and the symmetry routes retain $(-1)^{pq}$ because scalar factors have degree zero. These claims concern the simultaneous system construction and its flat-term K-flat total representatives, not only the evaluated maps.

Suppose the recursive $\beta_P,\beta_Q$ and their $\gamma$ are invertible. Under these specified comparisons the canonical completed tensor constraint is
$$\widehat a=\beta_Q^{-1}\mathcal L_W(a)\beta_P.$$
This identifies the actual completed quotient-model reassociation, action or signed symmetry with the limit of the displayed system map: inserting the defining counits in the quotient models yields the same total-complex formula, and their naturality permits moving an inserted counit through that formula. Its coherent reduction is the same map, namely
$$\gamma_Q\mathcal R_W(\widehat a)=a\gamma_P,$$
using the whole-system identity $e_{S_Q}\mathcal R_W\mathcal L_W(a)=a e_{S_P}$. Thus both constraint vertices and their arrows, including all quotient transitions and the actual action-unit normalization, are identified.

proof.text: Apply completedPrimitiveCounitComparison with the identity of W and reduction data S twice. Its counit_effective clause makes the counit invertible on every reduction object, because S.reduction_normalized supplies normalization. For arbitrary completed inputs X,Y, transport this counit isomorphism along S.reductionTensor.app (X,Y) by counit naturality. This makes the counit at T(RX,RY) invertible. Composing it with R(r_(X,Y)) proves that the contraction is invertible. This argument needs no tensor-normalization closure lemma.

proof.text: Expand the primitive tensor beta. Counit naturality for T(e_A,e_N) gives R(beta_AN) followed by e_T(A,N) equal to d_AN followed by T(e_A,e_N). Naturality of r, functoriality of tensor and composition of product morphisms then expand beta_source at the associator as r_L followed by L(T(gamma_AN,e_H)), and beta_target as r_R followed by L(T(e_A,gamma_NH)). These identities are proved as private helpers.

proof.text: For the associator, expand its already-defined quotient roof and cancel the outer r inverse with r. Substitute the preceding beta and gamma expansions. Tensor functoriality cancels d_NH inverse with d_NH. Naturality of the monoidal associator on e_A,e_N,e_H gives the beta square. For symmetry, cancel the outer realization isomorphisms and apply braiding naturality. For the two actions the beta square is functoriality of L applied to the defining action composite.
